lessons.title: Cameras recorders and viewing
objectives: Trace a basic CCTV signal path.
explanation: A CCTV system combines image capture, transport, recording or storage, and authorized viewing. IP cameras send digital video over a network to an NVR or video-management system; analog cameras commonly send video to a DVR for recording. Hybrid designs exist, so verify the actual equipment rather than relying on the name alone.

A visible live image does not prove recording, time accuracy, playback or export works. A complete handover test considers the customer’s agreed purpose and approved requirements. Camera resolution alone does not guarantee identification: lens, distance, angle, lighting and motion matter. All examples here are generic; AITS-specific acceptance criteria have not been supplied.
lessons.example: Synthetic system: two IP cameras connect to a PoE switch; the recorder and authorized viewing workstation share the permitted network.
lessons.exercise: Draw the path from a camera to stored footage and identify where recording could fail while live viewing still works.
lessons.model_response: Camera → switch/network → recorder → storage. A disk or recording-schedule problem can affect storage while live video remains visible.
key_points: Capture, transport, record and view are distinct
NVR and DVR describe common architectures
Test playback as well as live view

lessons.title: PoE cabling and equipment checks
objectives: Review power compatibility and cabling before connection.
explanation: Power over Ethernet can deliver power and data over compatible Ethernet cabling. Check both the device’s supported PoE type and the switch or injector’s capability. Do not assume every RJ45 port supplies power or every injector is standards-compatible. Manufacturer documentation takes priority for the actual model.

A switch has per-port limits and a total power budget. Compare planned loads against the documented budget, allowing for the manufacturer’s conditions and cable losses. Axis explains that typical and maximum camera consumption differ with features and operating conditions. Inspect cable category, route, terminations, labeling, damage and suitability for the environment. Never improvise mains wiring as part of a network exercise.
lessons.example: Four fictional cameras each require a documented maximum allocation of 15 W. Their total is 60 W; a 50 W usable budget is insufficient even before other loads.
lessons.exercise: Calculate the example load and list two checks beyond total watts.
lessons.model_response: 60 W exceeds 50 W. Also verify per-port support and the correct PoE type for every device.
key_points: Check PoE type and per-port limit
Inspect and label the cable path

lessons.title: Survey placement and installation preparation
objectives: Prepare a survey that connects camera purpose to site constraints.
explanation: Start with the intended task: observe an area, recognize activity or capture usable identification detail under agreed conditions. Record field of view, expected lighting, mounting constraints, cable route, weather exposure and maintenance access. Avoid assumptions about recording private areas or neighboring property; escalate privacy and lawful-purpose questions to the responsible reviewer.

Before installation, check model and quantities against the approved scope, inspect for damage and confirm compatible accessories. Verify that safe access and required permissions are ready. A drawing should label devices and cable routes clearly enough for another technician to follow. Do not treat a draft survey as permission to drill, energize or change a customer system.
lessons.example: A fictional entrance faces bright afternoon sunlight. A site review should test the relevant lighting conditions instead of accepting a clear indoor bench image.
lessons.exercise: Create a survey checklist with purpose, scene, route, power, privacy and access headings.
lessons.model_response: For each heading record known evidence, an unresolved question and the person who must confirm it; leave unknown measurements blank.
lessons.thai_summary: สำรวจตามวัตถุประสงค์ของภาพ ตรวจแสง เส้นทางสาย ความเป็นส่วนตัว และทางเข้าทำงานที่ปลอดภัยก่อนติดตั้ง
lessons.summary: Define the viewing task Check real site conditions Confirm scope and safe access

lessons.title: Faults maintenance and handover
objectives: Separate symptom diagnosis from authorized corrective work.
explanation: For a missing image, establish whether one camera or many are affected, when it began and whether live view or playback is missing. Observe authorized power/link indications and compare with a known-good path where permitted. Possible causes include power, cabling, addressing, authentication, stream compatibility and recording settings; do not jump straight to a factory reset.

Maintenance starts with approved intervals and model instructions. Review authorized health indicators, time accuracy, storage condition and image obstruction without changing settings unnecessarily. Handover evidence should identify devices, configuration versions, tests performed, results, limitations and open issues. Transfer credentials through the approved secure method, never in the ordinary completion report.
lessons.example: Only playback is missing for camera C2; live view works. Investigate recording schedule, storage and timestamps before replacing the camera.
lessons.exercise: Write a handover entry that records a passed live-view test and an unresolved playback problem.
lessons.model_response: C2 live view passed at 14:00 in the agreed scene. Playback unavailable for the requested period. Recording/storage review pending; acceptance not claimed.
key_points: Scope the symptom before changing equipment
lessons.thai_summary: เริ่มจากขอบเขตอาการ ตรวจสอบอย่างมีเหตุผล และบันทึกผลกับงานค้าง ห้ามรีเซ็ตหรือเปิดเผยรหัสผ่านโดยไม่มีการอนุญาต
